title: 05. Advanced Patterns: Mixing Concurrency Models
summary: Covers When to Mix Concurrency Models, Running Blocking Code in AsyncIO, Running AsyncIO from Threads, Hybrid Architecture Patterns, Complete Hybrid Application Example.

sections.title: 14.1 When to Mix Concurrency Models
sections.body:

```
║  │   │   Handle HTTP requests   ←─ I/O-bound, many connections     │    │  ║
║  │   │   Database queries       ←─ I/O-bound, async drivers        │    │  ║
║  │   │   External API calls     ←─ I/O-bound, concurrent           │    │  ║
║  │   │                                                              │    │  ║
║  │   └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘    │  ║

║  │   │                        │   │                            │       │  ║
║  │   │  • Blocking I/O libs   │   │  • CPU-bound tasks         │       │  ║
║  │   │  • Legacy sync code    │   │  • Image processing        │       │  ║
║  │   │  • Database (no async) │   │  • Data analysis           │       │  ║
║  │   │  • File operations     │   │  • ML inference            │       │  ║
║  │   └────────────────────────┘   └────────────────────────────┘       │  ║
║  │                                                                       │  ║

```

### Decision Matrix

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    WHICH CONCURRENCY MODEL TO USE?                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  Task Type              │ Primary Model    │ Secondary (if needed)          │
│  ───────────────────────┼──────────────────┼────────────────────────────── │
│  HTTP requests (async)  │ asyncio          │ ThreadPool (blocking libs)    │
│  Database (async driver)│ asyncio          │ ProcessPool (heavy queries)   │
│  Database (sync driver) │ Thread/Process   │ run_in_executor()            │
│  File I/O               │ aiofiles/asyncio │ ThreadPool (sync fallback)   │
│  Image processing       │ ProcessPool      │ asyncio (coordination)       │
│  ML inference           │ ProcessPool      │ asyncio (API layer)          │
│  Real-time streams      │ asyncio          │ ProcessPool (processing)     │
│  Legacy sync library    │ ThreadPool       │ asyncio wrapper              │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

diagrams.title: A hybrid architecture
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  loop["asyncio event loop — HTTP, websockets, DB"] -->|"run_in_executor"| tp["ThreadPool — blocking SDKs"]
  loop -->|"run_in_executor"| pp["ProcessPool — CPU-heavy work"]
  tp -->|"Future"| loop
  pp -->|"Future"| loop
diagrams.explain: Most real systems combine models: the event loop handles the many slow network conversations, a thread pool wraps libraries that only offer blocking APIs, and a process pool does the heavy computation. The loop awaits the executor futures, so it never blocks.

sections.title: 14.2 Running Blocking Code in AsyncIO
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Simulates blocking I/O operation
- CPU-intensive calculation
- Async wrapper for requests.get()
- Async wrapper for requests.post()
- Run blocking I/O in thread pool
- Run CPU-intensive in process pool
- Run multiple in parallel
- Create thread pool for sync operations

**Defines:** `blocking_io()`, `cpu_intensive()`, `main()`, `async_get()`, `async_post()`, `blocking_task()`

### Visual Explanation

```
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    RUN_IN_EXECUTOR                                          ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                             ║
║  Problem: Blocking code stops the event loop!                               ║
║                                                                             ║
║  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   ║
║  │   Event Loop Thread                                                  │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │   ║
║  │   │ async task 1                                               │     │   ║
║  │   │     │                                                      │     │   ║
║  │   │     ├──> await blocking_call()  ← BLOCKS EVERYTHING!      │     │   ║
║  │   │     │    ████████████████████                              │     │   ║
║  │   │     └──> continues                                         │     │   ║
║  │   │                                                            │     │   ║
║  │   │ async task 2: WAITING... :(                                │     │   ║
║  │   │ async task 3: WAITING... :(                                │     │   ║
║  │   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │   ║
║  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   ║
║                                                                             ║
║  Solution: run_in_executor()                                                ║
║                                                                             ║
║  ┌──────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐   ║
║  │   Event Loop     │    │              Executor Pool                   │   ║
║  │                  │    │                                              │   ║
║  │  async task 1 ───┼──► │  Thread 1: blocking_call() ████████████     │   ║
║  │  async task 2 ─► │    │  Thread 2: available                        │   ║
║  │  async task 3 ─► │    │  Thread 3: available                        │   ║
║  │                  │    │                                              │   ║
║  │  All tasks run!  │◄───┼── Returns result when done                  │   ║
║  └──────────────────┘    └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘   ║
║                                                                             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: Basic run_in_executor

```python
import asyncio
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, ProcessPoolExecutor

def blocking_io():
    """Simulates blocking I/O operation"""
    time.sleep(1)
    return "I/O complete"

def cpu_intensive(n):
    """CPU-intensive calculation"""
    return sum(i * i for i in range(n))

async def main():
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    # Create executors
    thread_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)
    process_pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)

    # Run blocking I/O in thread pool
    print("Running blocking I/O...")
    result1 = await loop.run_in_executor(thread_pool, blocking_io)
    print(f"I/O result: {result1}")

    # Run CPU-intensive in process pool
    print("Running CPU task...")
    result2 = await loop.run_in_executor(
        process_pool,
        cpu_intensive,
        10_000_000
    )
    print(f"CPU result: {result2}")

    # Run multiple in parallel
    print("Running parallel tasks...")
    tasks = [
        loop.run_in_executor(thread_pool, blocking_io),
        loop.run_in_executor(thread_pool, blocking_io),
        loop.run_in_executor(process_pool, cpu_intensive, 5_000_000),
    ]
    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
    print(f"Parallel results: {results}")

    # Cleanup
    thread_pool.shutdown(wait=False)
    process_pool.shutdown(wait=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: Wrapping Sync Library

```python
import asyncio
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from functools import partial
import requests  # Sync HTTP library

# Create thread pool for sync operations
sync_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10)

async def async_get(url, **kwargs):
    """Async wrapper for requests.get()"""
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    func = partial(requests.get, url, **kwargs)
    response = await loop.run_in_executor(sync_executor, func)
    return response

async def async_post(url, **kwargs):
    """Async wrapper for requests.post()"""
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    func = partial(requests.post, url, **kwargs)
    response = await loop.run_in_executor(sync_executor, func)
    return response

async def main():
    # Use sync library asynchronously
    urls = [
        "http://httpbin.org/get",
        "http://httpbin.org/headers",
        "http://httpbin.org/ip",
    ]

    # Parallel requests using sync library
    tasks = [async_get(url) for url in urls]
    responses = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

    for resp in responses:
        print(f"{resp.url}: {resp.status_code}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 3: asyncio.to_thread (Python 3.9+)

```python
import asyncio
import time

def blocking_task(name, duration):
    """Blocking function"""
    print(f"Starting {name}")
    time.sleep(duration)
    print(f"Finished {name}")
    return f"{name} done"

async def main():
    # Python 3.9+ simplified syntax
    # Uses default ThreadPoolExecutor

    # Single task
    result = await asyncio.to_thread(blocking_task, "Task1", 1)
    print(f"Result: {result}")

    # Multiple tasks in parallel
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        asyncio.to_thread(blocking_task, "TaskA", 1),
        asyncio.to_thread(blocking_task, "TaskB", 2),
        asyncio.to_thread(blocking_task, "TaskC", 1.5),
    )
    print(f"All results: {results}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

sections.title: 14.3 Running AsyncIO from Threads
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Worker thread that needs async functionality
- Thread with its own event loop
- Async function to be called from thread
- Submit coroutine to event loop (thread-safe)
- Wait for result (blocks this thread only)
- Let async tasks run while threads work
- Create new event loop for this thread
- Run async code in this thread

**Defines:** `async_fetch()`, `thread_worker()`, `main()`, `async_task()`, `thread_with_own_loop()`

### Visual Explanation

```
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    ASYNCIO FROM THREADS                                     ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                             ║
║  Scenario: Thread needs to call async code                                  ║
║                                                                             ║
║  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ║
║  │                                                                       │  ║
║  │   Main Thread (Event Loop)          Worker Thread                     │  ║
║  │   ─────────────────────────         ─────────────────                │  ║
║  │   │                                 │                                 │  ║
║  │   │  async def fetch():             │  def worker():                  │  ║
║  │   │      ...                        │      # Need to call fetch()!   │  ║
║  │   │                                 │      ???                        │  ║
║  │   │                                 │                                 │  ║
║  │   ▼                                 ▼                                 │  ║
║  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ║
║                                                                             ║
║  Solution 1: asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe()                            ║
║                                                                             ║
║  ┌────────────────┐                    ┌─────────────────┐                 ║
║  │  Main Thread   │                    │  Worker Thread  │                 ║
║  │                │                    │                 │                 ║
║  │  loop = get_   │                    │  future =       │                 ║
║  │    event_loop()│◄───────────────────│    run_coroutine│                 ║
║  │                │   submit coro      │    _threadsafe( │                 ║
║  │  [runs coro]   │                    │      coro, loop)│                 ║
║  │                │────────────────────│►                │                 ║
║  │                │   return result    │  result =       │                 ║
║  │                │                    │    future.result()               ║
║  └────────────────┘                    └─────────────────┘                 ║
║                                                                             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: run_coroutine_threadsafe

```python
import asyncio
import threading
import time

# Async function to be called from thread
async def async_fetch(url):
    await asyncio.sleep(1)  # Simulate network
    return f"Data from {url}"

def thread_worker(loop, url):
    """Worker thread that needs async functionality"""
    print(f"Thread {threading.current_thread().name}: Starting")

    # Submit coroutine to event loop (thread-safe)
    future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(
        async_fetch(url),
        loop
    )

    # Wait for result (blocks this thread only)
    result = future.result(timeout=10)
    print(f"Thread {threading.current_thread().name}: Got {result}")

    return result

async def main():
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    # Start worker threads
    threads = []
    for i in range(3):
        t = threading.Thread(
            target=thread_worker,
            args=(loop, f"http://example.com/{i}"),
            name=f"Worker-{i}"
        )
        threads.append(t)
        t.start()

    # Let async tasks run while threads work
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    print("Main: Doing other async work...")
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # Wait for threads
    for t in threads:
        t.join()

    print("Main: All threads completed")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: New Event Loop in Thread

```python
import asyncio
import threading

async def async_task(name):
    """Async task"""
    print(f"Task {name}: Starting")
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print(f"Task {name}: Done")
    return f"Result from {name}"

def thread_with_own_loop():
    """Thread with its own event loop"""
    # Create new event loop for this thread
    loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
    asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)

    try:
        # Run async code in this thread
        result = loop.run_until_complete(
            asyncio.gather(
                async_task("A"),
                async_task("B"),
            )
        )
        print(f"Thread results: {result}")
    finally:
        loop.close()

def main():
    # Start threads, each with own event loop
    threads = []
    for i in range(3):
        t = threading.Thread(
            target=thread_with_own_loop,
            name=f"AsyncThread-{i}"
        )
        threads.append(t)
        t.start()

    for t in threads:
        t.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

diagrams.title: Calling into a running loop from another thread
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant T as Worker thread
  participant L as Event loop thread
  T->>L: asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coro, loop)
  L->>L: schedule coro as a Task
  L-->>T: concurrent.futures.Future
  T->>T: future.result(timeout=5) blocks only this thread
diagrams.explain: asyncio objects are **not thread-safe**. From another thread, use `run_coroutine_threadsafe` (for coroutines) or `loop.call_soon_threadsafe` (for plain callbacks); calling `create_task` or touching an `asyncio.Queue` directly from a foreign thread causes subtle bugs.

sections.title: 14.4 Hybrid Architecture Patterns
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Heavy computation
- Handle compute request
- Handle fetch request (I/O-bound)
- CPU worker process
- CPU-intensive function (runs in process pool)
- Offload to process pool
- Simulate async work (e.g., fetching from API)
- Check queue in thread to not block

**Defines:** `process_data()`, `handle_compute()`, `handle_fetch()`, `create_app()`, `cpu_worker()`, `async_producer()`, `async_consumer()`, `main()`

### Pattern 1: AsyncIO + ProcessPool for CPU Tasks


### Code Example

```python
import asyncio
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
import aiohttp
from aiohttp import web
import json

# CPU-intensive function (runs in process pool)
def process_data(data):
    """Heavy computation"""
    result = sum(x ** 2 for x in range(data['iterations']))
    return {'input': data, 'result': result}

# Global process pool
process_pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)

async def handle_compute(request):
    """Handle compute request"""
    data = await request.json()

    # Offload to process pool
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    result = await loop.run_in_executor(
        process_pool,
        process_data,
        data
    )

    return web.json_response(result)

async def handle_fetch(request):
    """Handle fetch request (I/O-bound)"""
    url = request.query.get('url', 'http://example.com')

    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(url) as resp:
            text = await resp.text()

    return web.json_response({
        'url': url,
        'length': len(text)
    })

def create_app():
    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_post('/compute', handle_compute)
    app.router.add_get('/fetch', handle_fetch)
    return app

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app = create_app()
    web.run_app(app, port=8080)
```

### Pattern 2: Producer-Consumer Hybrid

```python
import asyncio
import multiprocessing as mp
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
import queue
import time

def cpu_worker(task_queue, result_queue):
    """CPU worker process"""
    while True:
        try:
            task = task_queue.get(timeout=1)
            if task is None:  # Poison pill
                break

            # CPU-intensive processing
            task_id, data = task
            result = sum(x ** 2 for x in range(data))
            result_queue.put((task_id, result))

        except queue.Empty:
            continue

async def async_producer(task_queue, num_tasks):
    """Async producer"""
    for i in range(num_tasks):
        # Simulate async work (e.g., fetching from API)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        task_queue.put((i, 100000))
        print(f"Produced task {i}")

    # Send poison pills
    for _ in range(4):
        task_queue.put(None)

async def async_consumer(result_queue, num_tasks):
    """Async consumer"""
    received = 0
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    while received < num_tasks:
        # Check queue in thread to not block
        try:
            task_id, result = await loop.run_in_executor(
                None,
                lambda: result_queue.get(timeout=0.1)
            )
            print(f"Consumed result {task_id}: {result}")
            received += 1
        except queue.Empty:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

async def main():
    # Create multiprocessing queues
    task_queue = mp.Queue()
    result_queue = mp.Queue()

    # Start worker processes
    workers = []
    for _ in range(4):
        p = mp.Process(target=cpu_worker, args=(task_queue, result_queue))
        p.start()
        workers.append(p)

    num_tasks = 20

    # Run producer and consumer concurrently
    await asyncio.gather(
        async_producer(task_queue, num_tasks),
        async_consumer(result_queue, num_tasks),
    )

    # Wait for workers
    for p in workers:
        p.join()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

sections.title: 14.5 Complete Hybrid Application Example
sections.body:
```python
"""
Hybrid Application: Web API with CPU-intensive processing
"""
import asyncio
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional
import aiohttp
from aiohttp import web
import time

# Executors
process_pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)
thread_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10)

# CPU-intensive functions (for process pool)
def analyze_text(text: str) -> dict:
    """CPU-intensive text analysis"""
    words = text.split()
    word_freq = {}
    for word in words:
        word_freq[word.lower()] = word_freq.get(word.lower(), 0) + 1

    # Simulate heavy computation
    time.sleep(0.5)

    return {
        'word_count': len(words),
        'unique_words': len(word_freq),
        'top_words': sorted(word_freq.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:10]
    }

def process_image(image_data: bytes) -> dict:
    """CPU-intensive image processing"""
    # Simulate heavy processing
    time.sleep(1)
    return {
        'size': len(image_data),
        'processed': True
    }

# Blocking I/O function (for thread pool)
def read_large_file(filepath: str) -> str:
    """Blocking file read"""
    with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
        return f.read()

# Async handlers
async def handle_analyze(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
    """Analyze text - uses process pool for CPU work"""
    data = await request.json()
    text = data.get('text', '')

    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    # Run CPU-intensive analysis in process pool
    result = await loop.run_in_executor(process_pool, analyze_text, text)

    return web.json_response(result)

async def handle_fetch_and_analyze(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
    """Fetch URL and analyze - combines I/O and CPU"""
    url = request.query.get('url')
    if not url:
        return web.json_response({'error': 'Missing url'}, status=400)

    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    # Async I/O - fetch URL
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(url) as resp:
            text = await resp.text()

    # CPU-intensive analysis in process pool
    result = await loop.run_in_executor(process_pool, analyze_text, text)

    return web.json_response({
        'url': url,
        'analysis': result
    })

async def handle_batch_process(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
    """Process multiple items in parallel"""
    data = await request.json()
    texts = data.get('texts', [])

    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    # Process all texts in parallel using process pool
    tasks = [
        loop.run_in_executor(process_pool, analyze_text, text)
        for text in texts
    ]

    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

    return web.json_response({
        'count': len(results),
        'results': results
    })

# Application setup
def create_app() -> web.Application:
    app = web.Application()

    # Routes
    app.router.add_post('/analyze', handle_analyze)
    app.router.add_get('/fetch-analyze', handle_fetch_and_analyze)
    app.router.add_post('/batch', handle_batch_process)

    return app

async def cleanup(app):
    """Cleanup on shutdown"""
    process_pool.shutdown(wait=True)
    thread_pool.shutdown(wait=True)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app = create_app()
    app.on_cleanup.append(cleanup)
    web.run_app(app, port=8080)
```

sections.title: Pitfalls & Gotchas
sections.body:
### Deadlock with run_coroutine_threadsafe

```python
# ❌ Deadlock! Event loop is blocked
async def bad_handler(request):
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    def blocking():
        # This blocks the event loop thread!
        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(
            some_async_func(), loop
        )
        return future.result()  # Deadlock! Loop can't run

    await loop.run_in_executor(None, blocking)

# ✅ Correct approach
async def good_handler(request):
    result = await some_async_func()
    return result
```

### Sharing State Between Processes

```python
# ❌ Can't share Python objects
shared_dict = {}  # Each process has its own copy!

# ✅ Use multiprocessing shared memory
import multiprocessing as mp
manager = mp.Manager()
shared_dict = manager.dict()
```
